newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian centre-right opposition worried by budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian centre-right opposition worried by budget.

text.p: Party leaders in the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc think the government's 1997 budget will be "unsatisfactory", the head of the small CDU party said after an alliance summit.
"News about the budget is worrying and we think it is largely unsatisfactory," Rocco Buttiglione told reporters at the end of the meeting held at the house of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi.
The government is expected to unveil the budget, which is forecast to cut 32.4 trillion lire off next year's deficit, by the end of the week.
But Prime Minister Romano Prodi has failed to persuade his hard-left ally, Communist Refoundation, to accept cuts to pensions and health care spending.
Parties backing Italy's centre-left government are due to meet at 1600 GMT today to try to thrash out a deal.

Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said he might be prepared to support a special "Maastricht tax" aimed at boosting Italy's bid to be among the founder members of the planned single European currency.
"We are the only country in Europe which to enter into Europe will increase taxes rather than cut spending," Buttiglione said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
